content.text: An informal fallacy is a mistake in the content of an argument, not its form. Spotting one takes judgment.

symbols.name: Attacking the person
symbols.meaning: Answers the arguer instead of the argument.

symbols.name: Distorting a view
symbols.meaning: Attacks a weaker version of what was said.

symbols.name: Changing the subject
symbols.meaning: Brings in a point that does not bear on the issue.

symbols.name: Too few options
symbols.meaning: Offers two choices when there are more.

symbols.name: A chain of doom
symbols.meaning: Claims one step leads to disaster, without evidence.

symbols.name: The wrong expert
symbols.meaning: Cites someone outside their field as proof.

examples.title: Ad hominem
lines: Dr. Smith says smoking causes cancer.
But Dr. Smith is paid by an anti-smoking group.
examples.conclusion: So smoking probably does not cause cancer.
examples.note: Who pays Dr. Smith does not touch the evidence. Answer the argument, not the person.

examples.title: Straw man
lines: A: We should have stricter pollution rules.
B: So you want to shut down every business?
examples.note: B attacks a view that A never held.

question.prompt: 'You can't trust John's case for recycling. He drives a big truck!' Which fallacy is this?
question.hint: Is the reply about John's reasons, or about John?
question.explanation: The reply attacks John's habits instead of his reasons. That is ad hominem.
